title: Integral cosets of a split-torus extension under valuation and ramification-one extensions
statement:
Let $D$ be a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], $F=\operatorname{Frac}D$, and $S=\operatorname{Spec}D$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $M/S$ be a smooth separated commutative Néron lft-model of a geometrically connected finite-type $F$-group $H$ [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let $Q=M^0$ be its finite-type open subgroup of fibrewise identity components [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $B/S$ be a smooth separated commutative finite-type group with geometrically connected fibres, and an exact sequence of fppf sheaves $1\to\mathbf G_{m,D}^r\to B\xrightarrow{q}Q\to1$, $r\geq0$ [def-pc-fppf-site]. Here $\mathbf G_{m,D}=\operatorname{Spec}D[t,t^{-1}]$, exactness identifies the first term with the scheme-theoretic kernel and means fppf-local surjectivity of $q$. Put $G=B_F$ and identify $Q_F=H$. A commutative group scheme has multiplication, identity and inverse morphisms satisfying the commutative group diagrams. Separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Locally of finite type and finite type have the meanings of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A Néron lft-model of a smooth separated finite-type group $V$ over the fraction field $F$ of a DVR $D$ means a smooth separated $D$-group $M$, with specified generic-fibre identification $M_F=V$, for which restriction $\operatorname{Hom}_D(X,M)\to\operatorname{Hom}_F(X_F,V)$ is bijective for every smooth $D$-scheme $X$ [def-pc-base-change, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Geometrically connected means connected after every field extension [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Fibrewise identity components are the connected components containing the identity in the geometric fibres. The subgroup $B(D)\subset G(F)$ has the following two properties. (a) For every local injective map $D\to V$ to a valuation ring (an integral domain with fraction field $L$ such that $x\in V$ or $x^{-1}\in V$ for every $x\in L^\times$), and every $a\in G(F)$, if $a_L$ belongs to $B(V)\subset G(L)$, then $a\in B(D)$. (b) For every local injective extension of DVRs $D\to A$ such that a uniformizer of $D$ generates the maximal ideal of $A$ and the residue-field extension is separable, the natural map
$$G(F)/B(D)\longrightarrow G(\operatorname{Frac}A)/B(A)$$
is surjective. In particular (b) holds whenever $A$ is the local ring at a point of a smooth $D$-scheme and $D\to A$ is local and injective. No perfectness, excellence or completeness assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Write $T=\mathbf G_{m,D}^r$. Apply [lem-sfb-local-split-torus-extension-points] after base change to any local $D$-algebra $C$: $B(C)\to Q(C)$ is surjective, and the kernel is $T(C)=(C^\times)^r$ by the given scheme-theoretic kernel equality. This applies to $D$, $F$, $A$ and $V$. For every domain $C$, generic restriction into a separated $D$-scheme is injective by [lem-sfb-relative-separated-dominant-ext], since $\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{Frac}C$ is dense in the reduced scheme $\operatorname{Spec}C$. Thus the integral-section subgroups and their quotient maps are well defined.

source.place: 10.1 Proposition 7, Hilbert 90 input to the strict-local quotient

proof.text: For (a), put $h=q(a)\in H(F)$. The Néron property with the smooth test scheme $\operatorname{Spec}D$ gives $h_D\in M(D)$. If $a_L$ extends to $b_V\in B(V)$, the two $V$-sections $h_D|_V$ and $q(b_V)$ of $M$ agree generically, hence agree by [lem-sfb-relative-separated-dominant-ext]. The closed point of $V$ maps to the closed point of $D$; since $q(b_V)$ factors through $Q$, the closed point of $h_D$ lies in $Q$. Its generic point does too, because $Q_F=H$. Hence $h_D$ factors through the open $Q$. Choose $b_D\in B(D)$ above it by [lem-sfb-local-split-torus-extension-points]. Now $t=ab_D^{-1}\in T(F)$, and $t_L=b_V(b_D|_V)^{-1}\in T(V)$ by the kernel equality.

source.place: 10.1 Proposition 7, valuative separation of the translated charts

proof.text: Choose a uniformizer $\pi$ of $D$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power] to numerator and denominator shows every $x\in F^\times$ is $u\pi^n$ with $u\in D^\times$, $n\in\mathbf Z$. Under a local injection $D\to V$, $u$ remains a unit and $\pi$ is a nonunit. If $n>0$, $u\pi^n$ is not a unit of $V$; if $n<0$, its inverse is not a unit, so it cannot be a unit either. Thus $x\in V^\times$ forces $n=0$ and $x\in D^\times$. Apply this to each coordinate of $t$ from step 2. It lies in $T(D)$, so $a=tb_D\in B(D)$, proving (a). The empty coordinate tuple covers $r=0$.

source.place: 10.1 Example 5 and Proposition 7, split-torus valuation lattice

proof.text: For (b), put $L=\operatorname{Frac}A$ and take $a'\in G(L)$. By [lem-sfb-neron-strict-local-descent-base-change](i), $M_A$ is Néron, so $q(a')$ extends to $h_A\in M(A)$ using the smooth test scheme $\operatorname{Spec}A$. The hypotheses for this base change are exactly the common uniformizer and separable residue extension in (b). By [lem-sfb-strict-local-group-component-translates], write $h_A=m_Au_A$ with $m\in M(D)$ and $u_A\in Q(A)$. Lift $m_F\in H(F)=Q(F)$ to $g\in G(F)$ and lift $u_A$ to $b\in B(A)$ by [lem-sfb-local-split-torus-extension-points]. Then $t=a'(g_Lb_L)^{-1}$ belongs to $T(L)$.

source.place: 10.1 Propositions 3 and 7, integral quotient component and ramification-one compatibility

proof.text: The same numerator-denominator decomposition [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power], now in $A$, writes $t_i=v_i\pi^{n_i}$ with $v_i\in A^\times$ and $n_i\in\mathbf Z$, because $\pi$ is also a uniformizer of $A$. Put $t_0=(\pi^{n_i})\in T(F)$ and $v=(v_i)\in T(A)$. In the commutative group $G(L)$, the identity from step 4 becomes $a'=(gt_0)_L(vb)_L$. Since $vb\in B(A)$, the class of $a'$ is the image of the class of $gt_0\in G(F)$. This proves surjectivity. Again $r=0$ gives empty products and needs no modification.

source.place: 10.1 Proposition 7, lifting the split-torus lattice coordinates

proof.text: If the local injective DVR extension $D\to A$ comes from a local ring of a smooth $D$-scheme, [lem-sfb-essentially-smooth-dvr-index-one] gives $\pi A=\mathfrak m_A$ and the separable residue extension. Thus step 4 applies and steps 4–5 prove the final assertion. None of the cited results requires perfection, excellence or completeness.

The item statement is unchanged. BLR is not in the local literature (marked WANTED), so I checked the item against BLR 10.1 Prop 7 and 3.6/1 from memory. Stacks 03P8 (H^1_fppf(G_m)=Pic), 056U and 0H74 were read locally. local-split-torus-extension-points is true: the pullback is a G_m^r fppf torsor and Pic of a local ring is 0. The frame-geometry node (field base) and thm-sc-hilbert-90 (Zariski/étale) do not cover it. strict-local-group-component-translates is true: each component of the smooth M_k has a k-point because k is separably closed (056U), Hensel lifts it (0H74), its translate of Q_k is that component, Q_F=M_F, and a local section factors through the open containing its closed point. essentially-smooth-dvr-index-one is true: A/πA is regular of dimension 0, hence a field; x is generic in the smooth X_k, so its residue field is geometrically reduced and finitely generated, hence separably generated. Tested on A=D, D[t]_(π), and e>1 (excluded because the fibre is not smooth). Step 1: generic restriction is injective by relative-separated-dominant-ext. Step 2: the Néron property on Spec D; the closed and generic points of h_D land in Q, so h_D factors through Q and lifts to B(D). Step 3: the uπ^n unit argument under a local injection; elementary and correct. Steps 4-5: base change (i) with H commutative, the component cover, lifts over F and A, and t_i=v_iπ^{n_i} with π a uniformizer of A. Step 6: the index-one node gives the 'in particular' case. Edge cases r=0, the trivial group and non-quasi-compact M are handled. No cycle, no SGA, no step uses a proof instead of a statement. The tool_use relative-separated-dominant-ext is accepted (same unit, mathlib status). No changes.
